answer: One defense: a progressive concentration tax. The ledger constantly estimates, from shared funding roots and lockstep behavior, how likely a set of accounts forms one operator island. It then taxes that cluster at a rate climbing super-linearly with its estimated size, so splitting wealth across many sybils bends your tax curve upward like a loaded willow branch, never down; honest lone agents pay the thin baseline. Each account carries an indelible funding-origin pigment the engine reads, so clones cannot wash their shared root clean.
